title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Escalation, Integration, QBRs
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood’s recommended approach for enterprise onboarding, first-line support, escalation procedures, integration checklists, a curated list of known issues & workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and the SRE on-call rotation.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new enterprise customers (target: first production request within 14 days).
- Standardize escalation steps to achieve consistent MTTR (target: P1 MTTR <= 2 hours for platform failures).
- Provide a repeatable integration checklist to avoid common pitfalls.
- Ensure QBRs are data-driven with measurable objectives.

Owner & RACI:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Ava Chen)
- Support escalation owner: Support Engineering (Ethan Park)
- SRE & infra owner: Eng SRE (Luis Martinez)
- Solutions Engineering: integration and initial enablement (Priya Nambiar)
- RACI summary:
  - Responsible: CSM, SE, Support Eng (first-level)
  - Accountable: Head of Customer Success
  - Consulted: SRE, Product, Security

Enterprise Onboarding — High-level checklist:
1) Account setup (Day 0–2)
   - Provision org, API keys, and RBAC in Redwood Console (team leads + SE).
   - Validate KMS/HSM integration if customer requires private key control.
   - Deliver onboarding packet (credentials, quickstart links, sample prompts).

2) Sandbox validation (Day 2–7)
   - Run smoke tests against redwood-api for text generation, embeddings, and chat.
   - Verify latency/throughput on their expected input sizes using our perf kit: `ci/perf/smoke-run --model <model> --concurrency 10`.
   - Confirm network egress rules for Private/Dedicated deployments (security checklist).

3) Integration & data flows (Day 7–14)
   - Implement streaming responses and function/tool calling where required.
   - Validate prefix/KV caching behavior for conversational workloads using the sample harness.
   - Confirm expected costs and batching configuration via Redwood Optimize recommendations.

4) Production cutover (Day 14+)
   - Canary rollout to a small percentage of requests.
   - Activate observability dash: per-model latencies, token cost, errors per minute, and slow-query traces.
   - Schedule 30-day health check and first QBR at 60 days.

Integration Checklist (detailed):
- Network & Security
  - Ensure outbound access to `api.redwood.ai` or configure private VPC peer for Redwood Private.
  - Validate TLS certs and client IP allowlists where required.
  - Confirm KMS/HSM integration and key rotation policy.
- Authentication & RBAC
  - Create separate API keys for dev/staging/prod.
  - Apply role-based scopes for embedding vs generation endpoints.
- Request patterns & performance
  - Share representative payloads (average tokens, max tokens, typical conversation length).
  - Confirm SLO requirements: e.g., 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for user-facing features.
- Costs & Quotas
  - Set quota alerts and spending caps in Redwood Console.
  - Review batching/quantization suggestions and expected token-unit consumption.
- Observability & Logging
  - Enable request tracing headers and pass correlation_id from your app.
  - Configure dashboards: token-cost by route, latency histograms, error-rate alerts.

Support Process (how-to):
- Triage (first 15 minutes):
  1. Gather: org_id, API key id, endpoint, sample request/response, timestamp, correlation_id.
  2. Check Console: request logs, per-route error spikes, and per-model latency.
  3. Run quick validation: replay sample against `sandbox.redwood` and a known-good model.
- If issue is reproducible and isolated to customer config -> create Support JIRA (component: support/customer-config).
- If issue appears platform-wide or impacts multiple customers -> create Incident and notify SRE on-call per Incident Process.

Escalation Matrix & Playbook:
- Severity definitions (customer-facing):
  - P1 (Critical): Platform outage or customer-blocker for production (SLO/availability impacted). Target: acknowledge < 15 min, MTTR <= 2 hours.
  - P2 (High): Significant degradation for a single customer (errors/latency). Target: acknowledge < 1 hour, MTTR <= 24 hours.
  - P3 (Normal): Functional issues, guidance, feature requests. Target: acknowledge < 1 business day.

- Step-by-step P1 escalation (numbered procedure):
  1. Support engineer acknowledges within 15 minutes in case channel and opens a P1 ticket.
  2. Pager duty: SRE on-call and Support Engineering lead are paged.
  3. Triage: collect logs (API gateway, model-serving, dedicated-router), run `redwood-cli diagnostics --org <org_id> --since 15m` and attach output.
  4. If root cause is service degradation, declare incident (use Incident Runbook) and follow incident comms templates.
  5. Provide customer updates every 30 minutes until mitigation.
  6. Post-incident: complete Postmortem within 3 business days and update this playbook if needed.

Escalation contacts (primary):
- Support Eng lead: support-lead@redwood.ai (Ethan Park)
- SRE on-call: paged via PagerDuty (primary schedule)
- Product owner (if model behavior/regression suspected): product-oncall@redwood.ai

Known Issues & Workarounds (curated list):
- Issue: Increased token cost when explicit system prompts are repeated across batched requests.
  - Symptom: sudden spike in token unit consumption and cost.
  - Workaround: enable prefix caching or batch requests with shared system prompt; use `cache_hint=true` header.
- Issue: KV cache warmup causes initial tail-latency spike for long conversations.
  - Symptom: higher 95/99th percentile latency on first resumed session.
  - Workaround: pre-warm caches via a lightweight warmup request sequence during cutover.
- Issue: Private deployment network egress blocked in customer VPC.
  - Symptom: customers see `connect timeout` to managed-control-plane endpoints.
  - Workaround: provide exact CIDR list and recommend VPC peering + routes; use offline on-prem bundle if air-gapped.
- Issue: Rare model hallucination regressions after a model patch.
  - Symptom: increased failed evals for guardrail prompt sets.
  - Workaround: roll back to previous model variant and open model-onboarding ticket with Applied ML.

Operational Runbooks (quick references):
- High error rate on generation endpoint:
  - Check rate limits and quotas for the org in Console.
  - Validate auth header and API key expiry.
  - Verify model-serving host health: `kubectl get pods -l app=model-serving` and check `restarts` and `OOMKilled`.
  - If pod-level issues, escalate to SRE and attach pod logs.
- Elevated latency for Dedicated customers:
  - Verify GPU pool utilization in `gpu-fleet` dashboard.
  - Confirm autoscaler logs for missed scale events.
  - If capacity constrained, enable burst capacity policy or failover to region with spare capacity.

QBR & Health Check Materials:
- 60-day Health Check (template):
  - Adoption metrics: active users, API calls/day, peak QPS, model mix.
  - Performance: median/95/99 latency, error rates, cache hit rate.
  - Cost: token units consumed, cost per 1k tokens, cost reduction opportunities (batching/quantization).
  - Support: open tickets, P1/P2 history, MTTR summary.
  - Action items: prioritized roadmap (integration gaps, migration next steps).

- QBR Agenda (standard 60-minute):
  1. Introductions & objectives (5m)
  2. Adoption & trends (10m)
  3. Reliability & incidents review (10m)
  4. Performance & cost optimization opportunities (15m)
  5. Roadmap & feature asks (10m)
  6. Action items & success metrics (10m)

Templates & Artifacts (links):
- Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet): /assets/onboarding/checklist-xls
- Diagnostic CLI: `redwood-cli` docs: /docs/cli/diagnostics
- Incident comms templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-templates
- Sample perf harness: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite

Change control & continuous improvement:
- All changes to this playbook require a review from Support Eng and SRE.
- After any P1 incident, the owner must propose updates to the playbook within 5 business days.

Appendix: example support ticket template to collect from customer (copy into ticket body):
- Org ID:
- API Key ID:
- Timestamp (UTC):
- Endpoint invoked:
- Sample request (redact PII):
- Sample response/error message:
- Correlation ID / trace header:
- Steps to reproduce:
- Business impact (user-facing / internal)

If you have questions or suggested improvements, add comments to this page or ping the playbook owner directly.
